headline: Cheaha State Park Lodging and Day Use
reservation: Day-use access is generally available at the gate, but the historic stone cabins, lodge, and improved campsites often book months in advance. The reservation system for Alabama State Parks is the official channel; verify availability for peak foliage weeks in October and November early in your planning cycle.

days.title: The Alabama Summit

stops.name: Bunker Tower
stops.detail: Climb this historic CCC stone tower at the highest point in Alabama for 360-degree views of Talladega National Forest.

stops.name: Bald Rock Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk this accessible wooden path to an overlook providing expansive views to the north and west.

days.driving: Minimal; these sites are located within the core park loop.
days.note: Boardwalk can be slippery when misty; proceed with caution during morning fog.

days.title: Rugged Ridge Hiking

stops.name: Pulpit Rock
stops.detail: Take a short but rocky hike down to this granite ledge for a dramatic perspective of the valley below.

stops.name: McDill-Hernandez Trail
stops.detail: Follow the ridgeline for deeper wilderness views and to see the historic plane wreckage site located along the path.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for local park road transfers; watch for cyclists and wildlife.
days.note: Sturdy hiking boots are essential due to the jagged quartzite terrain.

days.title: Lake and Lower Forest
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from Base of Mountain

stops.name: Cheaha Lake
stops.detail: Relax at the 6-acre lake at the mountain's base, suitable for a shaded picnic or a brief paddle.

stops.name: Pinhoti Trail Access
stops.detail: Walk a segment of this long-distance trail that connects the southern Appalachians through the Talladega Forest.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for the winding descent from the summit to the lake area.
days.note: The lake area is at a lower elevation and may feel significantly warmer than the summit.

intel.title: Summit Crowds
intel.text: The lot near Bunker Tower fills quickly on autumn Saturdays. Use the overflow parking near the lodge if the primary summit area is congested.

intel.title: Ridge Reception
intel.text: Service is often available at the summit but vanishes quickly on the Pinhoti Trail or near the lake. Do not rely on streaming for navigation in the forest.

intel.title: Last Gas Points
intel.text: Fuel up in Oxford or Lineville before starting the climb up Highway 281. There are no refueling stations once you enter the state park or the National Forest Scenic Drive.

intel.title: Clarity Windows
intel.text: Spring mornings often feature heavy valley mist. For the best photography from Bunker Tower, wait until the sun burns off the fog by late morning.

intel.title: Winter Road Closures
intel.text: Highway 281 (Skyway Parkway) can become treacherous with rime ice during winter storms. Verify road status with Alabama State Parks if freezing temperatures are forecast.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at BHM and drive east via I-20. Oxford offers the last major retail center for groceries and hiking supplies before the mountain ascent.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for the paved Skyway Parkway, but check for low-clearance warnings if planning to explore unpaved forest service side roads.
plan.goldenHour: Pulpit Rock is a traditional named spot for sunset, providing views of the sun dipping below the Talladega ridges.
